title: DLBFoam: An open-source dynamic load balancing model for fast reacting flow simulations in OpenFOAM
checked: full primary paper
researchQuestion: Reduce imbalance in cell chemistry integration without changing mesh ownership.
method: MPI chemistry-task redistribution; separately reference-cell filtering.
hardware: Mahti: dual 64-core AMD EPYC Rome nodes, HDR 200 Gb/s; Spray A comparison uses 256 MPI ranks.
benchmark: ECN Spray A, about 4.5 million cells; 500 timesteps, dt=2e-7 s, pre-ignition interval.
mainResult: Figure 11 reports 2.57x for load balancing alone and 9.87x with reference-cell filtering, relative to standard OpenFOAM for the stated case.
limitations: Combined filtering gain must not be attributed to balancing alone; different chemistry/hardware from this study.
relevance: Established task-only baseline; our static method also reallocates transport work and interfaces.
